question: Which 4 immune cell markers distinguish macrophages (Cluster 7) from T cells (Cluster 9) in the newborn lung?

nodes.label: Identify clusters corresponding to macrophages (7) and T cells (9) using provided cell type annotations in the newborn lung dataset
Subset the expression matrix to cells in macrophage Cluster 7 and T cell Cluster 9 for focused comparison
Perform differential expression analysis between macrophage Cluster 7 and T cell Cluster 9 to find significantly upregulated genes in each
Intersect differentially expressed genes with known canonical immune markers to identify macrophage-specific and T cell-specific candidates
Rank candidate markers by effect size, specificity, and expression robustness to select 2 macrophage and 2 T cell markers that best distinguish the clusters
Load newborn lung CELLxGENE AnnData object and identify clusters 7 and 9 using cell_type and cluster annotations in adata.obs
Subset AnnData to cells where cluster_id == '7' (macrophages) or cluster_id == '9' (T cells) and create a new AnnData with only these cells

Run differential expression using rank_genes_groups on the subset AnnData with groups=['7','9'], method='wilcoxon', and store upregulated genes per cluster with adjusted p-values and log2 fold changes

Load curated lists of canonical macrophage and T cell markers from an external reference (e.g. MSigDB, PanglaoDB) and intersect these with significantly upregulated genes (FDR < 0.05, log2FC > 0.5) for each cluster to obtain candidate macrophage- and T cell-specific markers

For intersected candidates, compute effect size (log2FC), cluster specificity (percentage of expressing cells per cluster), and mean expression per cluster, then rank and select the top 2 macrophage markers and top 2 T cell markers that best separate Cluster 7 from Cluster 9
